what: Medtronic makes medical devices: pacemakers and heart valves, surgical robots and stapling tools, spinal implants, brain stimulators and insulin pumps. Its products are implanted or used by surgeons in more than 150 countries.
customers: Hospitals, surgical centres and physicians, paid for by insurers and national health systems.
money: pacemakers, defibrillators, heart valves and stents
spine implants, neuromodulation and ear-nose-throat devices
surgical stapling, energy devices and the Hugo surgical robot
insulin pumps and continuous glucose monitors
moat: Surgeons train on specific devices and rarely switch, approvals take years, and hospitals buy across its whole catalogue under one contract.
risks: Growth has been slow compared with rivals such as Boston Scientific
Hospitals push back on device prices
Separating the diabetes business removes a growing unit
Product recalls and regulatory actions are a constant risk in devices
opportunities: The Hugo surgical robot gives it a position in a market Intuitive Surgical has dominated
Renal denervation for high blood pressure is a potentially large new category now reimbursed in the US
A dividend raised for decades supports the shares while growth is rebuilt
watch: Organic revenue growth by segment, and the commercial roll-out of Hugo and renal denervation.
